the_problem: Two fields hold the same concept under different names.
why_it_matters: Two fields with identical allowed values means two places to update and two answers to the same question.
resolution: Keep one. Delete the duplicate and repoint every rule.

the_problem: The word state means two unrelated things.
why_it_matters: A query or a report that says state is ambiguous and will eventually be read wrong.

the_problem: Journey means two different things in the same system.
fields_involved: assigned_journey (the plan we run), lead_state (where the student actually is)
why_it_matters: The team could not tell whether journey meant our plan or the student's position. This was the single biggest source of confusion.
resolution: Split the words. Our plan is a Playbook. Their position is a Journey stage.

the_problem: The same fact is stored in three places.
why_it_matters: Three copies drift apart. One says the link went out, another says it did not.
resolution: The event is the truth. The flag and the label are derived from it and are never written by hand.

the_problem: Opt out is stored in three places.
why_it_matters: A person could be suppressed in one place and messageable in another. This is a compliance risk, not a tidiness issue.
resolution: One switch. suppression_reason is the only field that gates a send.

the_problem: Invalid number is stored in three places.
why_it_matters: Same drift risk as opt out.
resolution: Derive all three from the delivery failure count.

the_problem: Attendance is stored both as a fact and as a position.
why_it_matters: The position should be calculated from the fact, not typed in separately.
resolution: Keep the facts. Calculate the stage.

the_problem: Three fields describe how keen someone is.
why_it_matters: Three numbers for one idea invites arguments about which is right.
resolution: Score is the only stored value. Temperature and priority are labels calculated from it at read time.

the_problem: Two source systems both claim to say where the lead came from.
why_it_matters: Marketing reports from UTM data and sales reports from the CRM source, and the two never agree.
resolution: source_detail is the business answer used by every rule. The UTM fields are attribution only and never drive a message.

why_it_matters: Overlapping values meant an active student could also read as a new lead.
resolution: existing_student_status answers whether they ever paid. previous_ssei_interaction answers what happened before that. Values no longer overlap.

the_problem: Provenance is split across two fields.
why_it_matters: Two fields answered one question: how much do we trust this.
resolution: Confidence is the answer. Source is kept as an audit detail only and never used in a rule.

the_problem: Three fields describe the exam date.
why_it_matters: Two of the three can be calculated from the first.
resolution: Store the target. Calculate the rest nightly.

why_it_matters: Unclear which one blocks the first message.
resolution: The resource ID is what gets delivered and what blocks. The campaign reference is reporting only.

the_problem: A derived value is stored and can go stale.
why_it_matters: It is calculated from the acquisition category, so storing it means it can disagree with the rule that produced it.
Two values mean the same outcome for messaging.
resolution: Collapse to invalid. Keep the bounce reason as a separate note.

the_problem: Offline access mixes a fact with a judgement.
why_it_matters: offline_accessible looked like captured data but is a rule output.
resolution: Distance is the fact. Accessibility is derived from a threshold that lives in one place.
